Connections

OBS connection

How to connect OBS (one-time setup)
  1. Open OBS Studio (version 28 or newer has this built in).
  2. In OBS's top menu, click Tools → WebSocket Server Settings.
  3. Tick Enable WebSocket server. Leave the port as 4455 and keep Enable Authentication ticked.
  4. Click Show Connect Info, then the Copy button next to Server Password.
  5. Back here, paste it into Password, tick Remember and click Connect. You can click OK in OBS to close its window.

OBS on a different computer? Put the Server IP from Show Connect Info into Host instead of localhost.

RØDECaster Duo (MIDI)

Connects automatically when the Duo is plugged in by USB. Pads must be set to the MIDI pad type on the Duo.

Press a pad on the Duo to see its message here.

How to set it up in VoiceAttack (2 minutes)
  1. Open VoiceAttack, click the pencil (Edit profile), then New Command.
  2. In When I say, type what you'll say (e.g. fire, become an orange, clear drawing).
  3. Click Other ▸ Windows ▸ Run an Application.
  4. Paste the Application and With these parameters lines from above (Copy buttons), and set the window to Hidden so nothing pops up.
  5. Click OK, OK, Done. Say it: TOS HUB does it.

Only works with the TOS HUB desktop app open. It listens on this PC only, and the secret part of the address stops other programs or websites using it.

⌨️ Keybinds · 💜 Channel points · 💎 Bits · ⚡ Power-ups

Hotkeys, channel points, bits and Power-ups are in the Triggers tab, and each can do several things: effects, OBS scenes, mute, recording… To have your voice, a gesture or Twitch press keys for you, use the Keybinds tab.

Twitch login optional

Only needed so TOS HUB can post shoutouts in your chat for you.

Log in so it can send shoutouts for you
  1. Go to dev.twitch.tv/console and click Register Your Application. Name: anything (e.g. “My TOS HUB”). OAuth Redirect URL: http://localhost. Category: Chat Bot. Client type: Confidential. Then click Manage and copy the Client ID.
  2. Paste the Client ID here, then log in:
  3. After you click Authorize, the new tab will say the site can't be reached. That's expected. Copy the whole address from that tab's address bar and paste it here:

In the TOS HUB app, a Twitch window opens when you click Log in with Twitch. Log in, click Authorize, and it closes by itself.

Your login is kept only in this browser on this computer and is only ever sent to Twitch.

First-time setup
  1. Connect OBS and your Duo on the Connections tab (it walks you through it).
  2. On the RØDECaster Duo, set each pad you want to use to the MIDI pad type. (Pads set to sounds or effects send nothing to this page.)
  3. Open this file in Chrome or Edge and click Allow when it asks to use MIDI devices.
  4. Click Quick setup and press your pads in order (or click any pad in the grid and press the matching pad on your Duo). Then click a pad and use + Add action to choose what it does.
  5. Keep this browser tab open while you stream (it can sit in the background). Use Backup now and then to save your pad setup to a file.

Live chat

Chat overlay preview

Change the look with Overlay settings (or hover the preview and click ⚙), then press Save in that menu. Turn on Demo mode there to see fake chatters.

Chat on my screen only you see it

A see-through chat window that floats over your game so you can read chat while you play. Your mouse clicks go straight through it, and it's hidden from OBS so it never shows on stream.

Alert sound (just for you)

So chat can't hear it, play it through a device OBS doesn't record, like your headphones or a separate output. In OBS, Settings → Audio shows which device Desktop Audio records: pick a different one here. On the RØDECaster, pick a spare virtual output (like “B”) and take its fader out of the USB 1 routing (Duo: Settings → Outputs → Routing). Then check it with “Can the stream hear my alert?” in Stream view.

Ctrl+Shift+C shows or hides it while you're in a game, and Ctrl+Shift+L lets you move it. It shows over games in borderless or windowed mode. In exclusive fullscreen Windows draws the game over everything, so switch the game to borderless.

Send to OBS

“Update” loads your saved overlay settings into that OBS source. “Create” adds a new WizHardz Chat source to the scene you're on. Do this again whenever you change the look.

Or add it to OBS by hand
  1. In OBS, add a Browser source, and untick Local file.
  2. Paste this into its URL box:
  3. Set the width and height (e.g. 600 × 1000) and tick Control audio via OBS if you use the overlay's sounds.

Only needed if chat-overlay.html isn't already in your TOS HUB folder. It comes in the app ZIP.

⌨️ Keybinds

Make TOS HUB press keys for you, set off by your voice, a hand gesture, your face or body, a mic sound, Twitch or another key. The keys go to whatever is in front (your game, Discord, a soundboard), or straight to OBS as an OBS hotkey. Each card reads Press … ← when …; click one to change it.

Want a key on your keyboard to set off an effect or OBS action instead? That's a ⌨️ Hotkey in the Triggers tab. Pressing keys works in the desktop app on Windows; a few games with anti-cheat ignore keys from other programs, so test it in yours.

Camera

TOS HUB opens your webcam itself and sends the finished cam (picture, frame, shape and effects) to OBS as one source. Face effects and face follow work on every frame, perfectly in sync. Keep TOS HUB open while you stream.


          
Works with a GoPro HERO9 or newer (your HERO10 Black included), with no GoPro app needed. Switch it on and plug it in with a USB-C cable that carries data (the one that came with it is fine). Nothing to change on a HERO10: it has no USB setting, just plug in. Only a HERO9 has Preferences → Connections → USB Connection, which needs to be on GoPro Connect. The first time, Windows may ask if TOS HUB can use networks: click Allow, because that's how the camera sends its picture over USB. For long streams, GoPro suggests taking the battery out and running it on USB power, so it stays cooler.

          

            
            
            
            
          

          

          
Camera tips: falling asleep, running hot
          
If your camera has its own sleep timer (OBSBOT cameras have Auto Sleep in OBSBOT Center), turn it off or set it long. TOS HUB will also wake the camera if it freezes or goes black (it gives up after 3 tries in case it's overheating). Camera running hot? 720p at 30 fps is much easier on it, and TOS HUB rests it when OBS isn't showing it.

Full-screen effects
          
Effects can also fill your whole stream (right over your game), not just your cam. TOS HUB adds one see-through layer to OBS for this; it sits on top and stays empty until an effect plays.

          

          

          
Then switch the effect buttons under the preview to 🖥️ Whole screen, or pick a Whole screen action in the Triggers tab. Works for sparkles, zap, fire, frost, boom, hearts, confetti, magic circle, portal, meteor, bubbles and smoke.

Teach TOS HUB your own hand signs: 🤘 rock on, 🤙 call me, 👌 OK, 🤞 crossed fingers, anything. Hold it up to the camera and click Record; it learns it in about a second. Then use it in Triggers (Tracking → Hands) or Keybinds like any other gesture. Works with either hand.

            

            

            

          

          

            
Teach TOS HUB your own poses: a superhero landing, the floss, pointing at chat, anything with your arms. Strike the pose, click Record, hold it for a second. Use it in Triggers (Tracking → Body) or Keybinds. Needs your shoulders, elbows and hands in shot.

    Auto clips
          
          
    
            
    
          
    
          
    Uses OBS's Replay Buffer (OBS → Settings → Output → Replay Buffer). The clip includes the seconds before the moment.
    
          
    
        
    
        
    Become an object
          
    Turn into a real thing that talks with your own eyes and mouth. Pick one to stay as it, or use the 🍊 Become an object effect (pads, chat, poses) for 12 seconds as a random one. Needs the ✨ TOS HUB camera and face tracking.
    
          
    
          
    
          
          
    Add any picture: click ＋ My own picture, drag one onto the grid, or copy a picture (e.g. right-click → Copy image on a website) and press Ctrl + V here. TOS HUB's AI cuts the thing out of its background by itself, and it stays on this PC.

    Works best when the camera can see you from the waist up. Hold a pose for a moment to set it off. Body effects show on your real picture (with an avatar on, its arms copy yours instead). The glowing aura looks best with the background cut out, because it then shines from behind you. Your body never leaves this computer.

    🖥️ Two PCs
    
      
    Stream from one PC and play on another. Install TOS HUB on both: the streaming PC runs everything here (OBS, Twitch, chat, webcam, pads); the gaming PC presses keys in your game, listens for your keybinds while you play, and can show the stream's effects over your game so you see what chat sees.
    
      
    
        
        
        
      
    
      
    
    
    
    
    
      
    🎮 Gaming PC
    
      
    Waiting for your gaming PC…
    
      
    
        
    On the gaming PC: open TOS HUB → Stream → Two PCs → This is my gaming PC. It finds this PC by itself; type this code there:
    
        
    
        
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
    While linked, ⌨️ Press keys actions press keys on the gaming PC, and your ⌨️ Keyboard triggers listen to the gaming PC's keyboard. If the link drops, both go back to this PC until it's back.
    
        
      
    
      
    
      
      
      
      
        Can't link? (Windows Firewall)
        
      The first time, Windows asks whether TOS HUB may use the network: tick Private networks and allow it. For the effects over your game, the gaming PC also talks straight to OBS on this PC, so OBS needs the same OK (OBS → Tools → WebSocket Server Settings must be on). Both PCs need to be on the same home network.
